taxonomyNote: Often lumped in Pseudacris regilla in older literature (Montana Field Guide: material before 2022 calls it Pacific treefrog); NatureServe notes nuclear DNA (Barrow et al. 2014) did not support the three-species split and Hyliola is a disputed genus.
fieldMarks: Toes are long with large disks and very little webbing.
Nearly all have a black stripe from the snout through the nostril, eye and eardrum to just above the front leg.
Back commonly tan mottled with dark brown spots; can be solid green or other colours.
Often heard but not seen; tadpoles have eyes outside the outline of the body from above.
behavior: Females can lay 500-750 eggs in total; clutches of a few cm hold 18-119 eggs (mean 68 in northwest Montana).
Breeds in shallow water of marshes, lakes, ponds and ditches; spends most of its time on the ground and may bask on woody plants far from water or climb into trees.
habitat: Grassland, chaparral, woodland, forest and farmland; on land except when breeding.
Eggs are laid in shallow marshes, lakes, ponds, ditches, reservoirs and slow streams.
range: Central California, Nevada, eastern Oregon, Idaho and western Montana, possibly extreme northwestern Utah; genetic work (Jadin et al. 2021) found it, not the Pacific treefrog, in Idaho and Montana.

lookalikes.name: Pacific treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Distinguishable only by genetics (Montana Field Guide).
